Recommended Highlights This Week

1. Singapore Tennis Open (WTA 500) – 21–27 September, OCBC Arena

2. #RevUpSG Azerbaijan GP Screening – 25–26 September, Kampung Admiralty

3. Lilytopia – final days, closes 27 September

4. Art Remembers exhibition – closes 27 September, National Gallery Singapore

5. Le Ju Xuan opens – Marina Bay Sands

F&B Promotions

Current dining promotions across our Shangri-La Group properties in Singapore:

Shangri-La Singapore

Beng Hiang brings nearly 48 years of Hokkien heritage to the Garden Terrace, with recipes passed down from the original Chinatown shophouse. Signatures worth flagging to guests include Orh Nee (yam paste dessert) and Hae Bee Hiam (spicy dried shrimp sambal) – dishes that rarely appear on hotel menus outside a genuine Hokkien kitchen.

  • Beng Hiang – Authentic Hokkien Cuisine, Garden Terrace.

Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa

  • Rasa Private Beach BBQ – SGD 188++ per package (2 adults + 2 children). Valid through 31 December 2026.

Hotel Jen Tanglin

  • J65 – International Seafood Dinner Buffet. $88++/adult, $44++/child. Shangri-La Circle members: 20% off.

Hotel Jen Orchard Gateway

  • Makan@JEN – daily lunch and dinner buffet, $30–55++ per person. 15% off for OCBC cardmembers, ongoing.

Events & Festivals

Overall Summary

This is a strong closing week for several longer-running recommendations: Lilytopia at Gardens by the Bay, the Art Remembers exhibition at National Gallery Singapore, and Gardens by the Bay's Mid-Autumn lantern display all wrap up on the 27th. On the sporting side, the newly upgraded Singapore Tennis Open – now a WTA 500 tournament – runs all week at OCBC Arena, and the Formula 1 build-up continues with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix community screening at Kampung Admiralty. On the dining front, Marina Bay Sands has opened Le Ju Xuan, a 188-seat family-style Chinese restaurant with one of Singapore's largest baijiu collections.

Singapore Tennis Open (WTA 500)

Following a successful WTA 250 debut last year, the Singapore Tennis Open has been upgraded to WTA 500 status for 2026 – placing it among the top tier of tournaments on the women's tennis calendar. The week-long tournament brings top-ranked players to OCBC Arena at The Kallang, with single-session tickets accessible from just $8.

Event Date: 21–27 September 2026

Location: OCBC Arena, The Kallang

Admission: From $8 per session

Best For: Tennis Fans / Sports Enthusiasts

Concierge Recommendation: A genuine step up from last year's tournament – worth mentioning the WTA 500 upgrade specifically to any guest who followed last year's debut, since it signals a meaningfully bigger field this time.

#RevUpSG – Azerbaijan Grand Prix Screening

The next stop in the #RevUpSG community watch party series ahead of the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix, bringing live race coverage to a heartland setting with a festival atmosphere, interactive games and F1 merchandise giveaways.

Event Date: 25–26 September 2026

Location: Kampung Admiralty

Admission: Free

Best For: Motorsport Fans / Free Activities / Families

Concierge Recommendation: A good free option for F1 fans staying further north – part of the same build-up series that's been running monthly since August.

Art Remembers – Closing Soon

A thought-provoking exhibition at National Gallery Singapore's City Hall Wing, bringing together twenty contemporary works by artists from across Southeast Asia. Rather than presenting mainstream historical accounts, the featured works reframe the artist's role from creator to archivist – each piece digs into archives to surface forgotten, lesser-known or marginalised histories from the region.

Event Date: Closes 27 September 2026

Time: 9:00am–9:00pm

Location: National Gallery Singapore, City Hall Wing

Admission: From $12/adult

Best For: Art Lovers / Culture Seekers / Something Reflective

Concierge Recommendation: A good closing-week recommendation for guests wanting something more contemplative than a typical exhibition – the framing of “artist as archivist” gives visitors a genuine angle to engage with, not just art to look at.

Restaurants & Bars

Le Ju Xuan

Marina Bay Sands' newest in-house Chinese restaurant has opened in the Hotel Tower 2 lobby, taking over the spot where Blossom once stood. Le Ju Xuan (乐聚轩) leans into family-style dining, drawing on Cantonese, Northern Chinese and Sichuan traditions under one roof – everything from handmade noodles and dumplings to premium live seafood. The restaurant also carries one of Singapore's largest baijiu collections, with around 70 labels including rare, aged Kweichow Moutai expressions.

Location: Hotel Tower 2 Lobby, Marina Bay Sands

Hours: Sun–Thu 11:00am–10:30pm; Fri–Sat (confirm closing time when booking)

Signature: Marble Goby (from $15/100g); Mapo Tofu with Minced Pork ($16.80); Braised Sea Cucumber, Fish Maw & Stuffed Bamboo in Superior Yellow Broth ($42.80)

Best For: Families / Groups / Chinese Cuisine Fans / Baijiu Enthusiasts

Concierge Recommendation: A strong pick for larger groups or families wanting variety under one roof – the baijiu collection specifically is worth mentioning to guests with an interest in spirits, since it's a genuinely rare depth for a restaurant setting rather than a dedicated bar.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Whole Earth

A long-standing name in Singapore's vegetarian dining scene, Whole Earth blends Peranakan and Szechuan influences into a fully plant-based menu – built to satisfy guests who wouldn't necessarily seek out vegetarian food, not just those who already do. The restaurant has held a Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition for its approachable, flavour-forward take on meat-free cooking.

Current Promotion: None advertised – check for seasonal set menus.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required to book.

Hours: Daily, 11:30am–2:30pm & 6:00pm–10:00pm (confirm current hours when booking)

Address: 76 Peck Seah Street, Singapore 079331

Signature: Buddha Jumps Over the Wall (vegetarian version); Otah

Concierge Recommendation: A good option to offer any guest with dietary restrictions who's worried about a limited menu – this is genuinely satisfying food, not a compromise.

Beirut Grill

A dependable name for Middle Eastern and Lebanese cuisine in Singapore, built around charcoal-grilled meats, fresh mezze and hand-made bread. The setting leans casual and communal – designed for sharing plates across a table rather than individually plated courses.

Current Promotion: None advertised – check for set menu options.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required; walk-ins generally accommodated.

Hours: Daily, lunch and dinner service (confirm current hours when booking)

Signature: Mixed Grill Platter; freshly baked pita with hummus and mutabal

Concierge Recommendation: A good group-dining recommendation for guests who enjoy sharing plates – suggest ordering a mix of mezze first before the grilled mains arrive.

Hotel & Hospitality News

No new hotel or leadership announcements to report this week – all previously featured properties remain unchanged. Colleagues should continue monitoring for updates ahead of NoMad Singapore's late-2026 opening.

Transport & Operational Updates

Sentosa Gateway Tunnel – Overnight Closure

The Sentosa Gateway Tunnel will close overnight on 21 September, 12:00am–5:00am, for routine tunnel washing works. Slip roads from Sentosa Gateway to Lower Delta Road and Keppel Road will be affected, with traffic diverted via Telok Blangah Road and Keppel Road. This is a brief, late-night closure unlikely to affect typical guest travel to or from Sentosa.

Overnight Expressway Works Continue

Several routine overnight closures continue this week, all between 12:00am and 5:30am: TPE/PIE slip roads near Tampines Ave 7 and Loyang Ave (21–25 September); KPE Tunnel slip roads on 21 and 23 September; MCE Tunnel slip roads on 24 September; and the PIE(Tuas) Exit 26A slip road on 27 September. Lentor Avenue's nightly closures (1:30am–5:30am) also continue through the month. None of these affect typical guest activity, but worth knowing for anyone with a very early or overnight transfer.

Closing Attractions – Final Weekend Crowds

Expect heavier footfall at Gardens by the Bay and National Gallery Singapore through the weekend of 26–27 September, as Lilytopia, the Mid-Autumn lantern display and the Art Remembers exhibition all close on the 27th.

Looking Ahead

Grand Prix Season Singapore 2026

The city-wide build-up to the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix begins in earnest from 2 October, with race-themed lifestyle experiences planned across multiple precincts ahead of the race itself on 9–11 October.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Lilytopia, Art Remembers and the Gardens by the Bay Mid-Autumn lantern display all close 27 September – this is a final call, not a routine mention.

  • The Singapore Tennis Open's upgrade to WTA 500 status is worth mentioning specifically to guests who ask – it signals a stronger field than last year's WTA 250 debut.

  • Le Ju Xuan's Friday/Saturday closing hours weren't independently confirmed this edition – verify directly before booking a late dinner.

Suggested Itineraries

Half Day — Last Call at the Gardens

Afternoon: Lilytopia at the Flower Dome – final days before it closes on the 27th.

Evening: Gardens by the Bay's Mid-Autumn lantern display, also closing the same day.

Tip: Both are in the same general area, so guests can comfortably fit both into one visit without needing separate transport.

Full Day — Sport & Art

Afternoon: Singapore Tennis Open at OCBC Arena – single-session tickets make this an easy add-on even for guests without much tennis background.

Evening: Art Remembers at National Gallery Singapore, then dinner at Le Ju Xuan or Whole Earth nearby.

Tip: OCBC Arena and the Civic District are a short taxi ride apart – easy to combine both halves of the day without much transit time.

2 Days — Marina Bay & Civic District

Day 1

Afternoon: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark, then dinner at Le Ju Xuan. Evening: Ce La Vi for a nightcap, same building.

Day 2

Morning: Art Remembers at National Gallery Singapore. Afternoon: Singapore Tennis Open at OCBC Arena.

Tip: Staying within Marina Bay for Day 1 avoids unnecessary transport – everything from SkyPark to Le Ju Xuan to Ce La Vi is within the same complex.

Quick Reference

Best Last-Chance Pick: Lilytopia (closes 27 September)

Best Sporting Event: Singapore Tennis Open (WTA 500)

Best Free F1 Activity: #RevUpSG Azerbaijan GP Screening

Best Closing Exhibition: Art Remembers

Best New Restaurant: Le Ju Xuan

Best Vegetarian Dining: Whole Earth

Best Group Dining: Beirut Grill
